Lantern protocol

This article relies on a single source. (May 2026)

Lantern is a protocol and an API for reading notes from knowledge bases over a slow link.[1] It was written for field stations that sync once a day, and it trades latency for a very small message format.

A Lantern session opens with a hello message, sends one request per note, and closes when the queue is empty. Each request names the note by its content hash, so a retried request can never fetch the wrong note.

History[edit]

The first version was drafted in 2019 and revised twice after field trials showed that batching requests saved more time than compressing them.
